reason: The caps seem suited to sealing the core's working windows, and this is the only available action.
expectation: I expect the caps to close the liner for storage, though I don't yet know whether further preparation will be needed.

effect: The caps closed the working ports while preserving the body-bearing core and neighboring ice for qualified cold storage until flight transfer.
reaction: It is reassuring that the surrounding ice will travel with the specimen, though the closure itself was straightforward.

mostWorthwhile.text: Closing the case was worthwhile because it secured both the specimen and its surrounding layer for storage.

leastWorthwhile.text: The closure was the only action and offered little decision-making, although its purpose was clear.

surprise.text: Nothing in this chapter particularly surprised me; the result matched my expectation.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary: the liner caps were a natural way to close the working ports.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to learn what happens when the core reaches the receiving laboratory, although this chapter itself offered little to explore.
